hints: A cable is safe to remove if there is another way around it — i.e. it sits on a cycle. How could a single DFS tell whether the part below a cable can 'climb back up' without using that cable?

Tarjan's bridge-finding: DFS giving each server a discovery time disc and a low value = the earliest discovery time reachable from its subtree using at most one back edge. Tree edge (v, u) is critical when low[u] > disc[v].

1. Build an adjacency list; set all disc to -1.
  2. dfs(v, parent): set disc[v] = low[v] = timer++.
  3. For each neighbour u ≠ parent: if unvisited, dfs(u, v), then low[v] = min(low[v], low[u]), and if low[u] > disc[v] record [v, u].
  4. If already visited, low[v] = min(low[v], disc[u]).
  5. Call dfs(0, -1).

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Remove each cable in turn and check with BFS/DFS whether the network is still connected.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One Tarjan DFS computing discovery times and low-links finds every bridge.

explain: With links [0,1],[1,2],[2,0],[1,3]: DFS from 0 visits 1 (disc 1), then 2 (disc 2), which sees 0 through a back edge, so low[2]=0 and low[1]=0. Then 1 visits 3 (disc 3); 3 has no other way back, so low[3]=3 > disc[1]=1 and [1,3] is critical. The triangle edges all have low values ≤ the parent's disc, so they are not. Skip only the parent node (fine here since there are no duplicate cables).
recognize: 'Which single edge, if removed, disconnects the graph?' → bridges via Tarjan's low-link DFS.
